findings.detail: Formal equal pay claim submitted by trade unions is proceeding through tribunal. Preliminary hearing held November 2025. Main hearing scheduled February 2027 will assess the validity of the council's job evaluation scheme. If found inadequate, a second hearing will determine if comparator jobs are of equal value, potentially triggering back-pay liability.
findings.matters: Equal pay litigation can result in material back-pay liabilities and ongoing cost implications; outcome depends on tribunal assessment of scheme validity, with financial exposure currently unquantified.
findings.figures: Hearing scheduled February 2027; financial exposure not yet quantified
findings.quote: the job evaluation scheme will be assessed and if it is considered to be a valid scheme the claims will fall away. If the Tribunal find that the scheme is not adequate then the Tribunal will list a further hearing to determine whether or not the claimants and the comparator jobs are of equal value

findings.paper_title: Risk Management Progress Report - Appendix 1 Risk in Focus Review - SRR-08 Financial Sustainability - Review Schedule 02 Period 02
findings.headline: Finance team relying on three interim arrangements to deliver critical government returns and accounts functions
findings.detail: Long-standing vacancies remain in the corporate finance team covering production of government returns, statement of accounts delivery, and reconciliation and control functions. These are being filled by interim arrangements (3 interim positions). Further recruitment is planned for 2026/27.
findings.matters: Critical financial functions that underpin statutory reporting and budget management are being delivered by interim staff rather than permanent expertise, creating continuity risk and potential for gaps in financial controls or reporting quality.
findings.figures: 3 interim arrangements in place; additional recruitment planned
findings.quote: A number of interim arrangements are in place (3-interim arrangements) to ensure these functions are delivered

findings.paper_title: Risk Management Progress Report - Appendix 1 Risk in Focus Review - SRR-08 Financial Sustainability - Review Schedule 02 Period 02
findings.headline: Q3 forecast shows potential shortfall in 2025/26 transformation investment at risk of not being deployed
findings.detail: Q3 forecast position indicates transformation investment for 2025/26 may be lower than planned. This is 'under review to ensure there is no adverse impact on the councils transformation programme and savings plan.' The council is relying on the Government's capitalisation exceptional financial support directive to fund this transformation investment.
findings.matters: If transformation investment undershoots while savings targets are already missed by £7.6m, the council's ability to achieve future-year savings targets and financial sustainability deteriorates significantly.
findings.figures: 2025/26 transformation investment; quantum of potential shortfall not disclosed
findings.quote: the Q3 forecast position indicates there is potential for the 2025/26 transformation investment to be lower than expected and this position is under review to ensure there is no adverse impact on the councils transformation programme and savings plan

findings.paper_title: Risk Management Progress Report - Appendix 1 Risk in Focus Review - SRR-08 Financial Sustainability - Review Schedule 02 Period 02
findings.headline: Government funding settlement confirms three-year settlement with 'significant' reduction in funding despite reduced uncertainty
findings.detail: Final settlement announced February 2026 provides three-year visibility for 2026-27, 2027-28 and 2028-29. While the multi-year settlement reduces immediate uncertainty compared to annual settlements, the council states the funding reduction itself 'has had a significant impact' on its financial planning.
findings.matters: Known funding reductions force greater reliance on savings delivery and transformation; when combined with the £7.6m savings slippage already evident, reduced funding narrows the council's options for managing the financial position over the MTFP.
findings.figures: Three-year settlement 2026-27 to 2028-29; specific funding reduction amount not quantified in this paper
findings.quote: Provisional settlement announced December 2025 and final settlement February 2026 has been announced and the 3-year settlement included within 2026-27, 2027-28 and 2028-29 budget / MTFP. This has reduced the amount of uncertainty over this period, but the reduction in funding has had a significant impact

findings.paper_title: Risk Management Progress Report - Appendix 1 Risk in Focus Review - SRR-08 Financial Sustainability - Review Schedule 02 Period 02
findings.headline: General Fund reserves drawn down £2.881m with council acknowledging continued drawdown is unsustainable
findings.detail: Q4 outturn shows £2.881m withdrawal from General Fund reserves, reducing the fund to approximately £29.6m. While this remains above the statutory minimum of £25m, the council explicitly states 'Continued reliance on reserves not sustainable in medium term' and is developing a recovery plan.
findings.matters: Unsustainable reserve drawdown signals the council is funding recurring expenditure with one-off resources; combined with £7.6m savings slippage, this trajectory becomes critical within 2–3 years.
findings.figures: £2.881m drawdown; General Fund now c.£29.6m; minimum requirement £25m
findings.quote: Q4 outturn confirms use of £2.881m of General Fund. General Fund reduces to c.£29.6m but remains above minimum level (£25m). Continued reliance on reserves not sustainable in medium term

findings.paper_title: Risk Management Progress Report - Appendix 1 Risk in Focus Review - SRR-08 Financial Sustainability - Review Schedule 02 Period 02
findings.headline: Material non-delivery of £7.6m in transformation savings slippage identified as primary driver of financial pressure
findings.detail: Draft outturn for 2025/26 confirms £7.6m of material non-delivery and slippage on transformation savings. The council explicitly identifies this as 'a primary driver of the overall financial position'. Delivery of remaining savings remains dependent on programme pace, capacity and organisational change capacity.
findings.matters: A council unable to deliver its planned savings programme faces a growing structural deficit; if £7.6m is already lost in 2025/26, future years' savings targets become harder to achieve, increasing the risk of a balanced budget requirement breach.
findings.figures: £7.6m material non-delivery/slippage of savings
findings.quote: The draft outturn position confirms material non-delivery/ slippage of savings (£7.6m). This is a primary driver of the overall financial position

findings.headline: Finance systems remain legacy and inadequate; new implementation planned for April 2028 with procurement starting December 2026
findings.detail: The council is working with digital teams on interim solutions to legacy system issues. Procurement for new finance systems has a target date of December 2026, with implementation not expected until April 2028. This represents a two-year window of transitional financial systems during a period requiring robust financial control.
findings.matters: A two-year transition period to new finance systems, starting from documented finance function capacity constraints, compounds financial control and reporting risk.
findings.figures: Procurement December 2026; implementation April 2028
findings.quote: Continue work with digital to identify interim solution to legacy system issues. Develop requirements and start procurement. Implement new solutions.

findings.headline: Committee reports submitted at statutory deadline with insufficient time for statutory officer input, and key decisions added to forward plan at latest possible date
findings.detail: Committee reports consistently arrive at or approaching statutory deadline, leaving inadequate time for scrutiny and early input from statutory officers. Key decisions are often added to the Leader's forward plan at the latest possible moment or moved within the plan, creating additional pressure and reducing time for public engagement.
findings.matters: Compressed timelines for statutory officer review of decisions — especially financial ones — indicate governance process weakness during a period of financial stress.
findings.figures: Reports at "statutory deadline" with "no adequate time for scrutiny"
findings.quote: Committee reports continue to be submitted at or approaching the statutory deadline, which does not adequately allow for scrutiny and input of advice from the Council's statutory officers. Further, while key decisions are published 28 days ahead of the decision being taken, these decisions are often added to the Leader's forward plan at the latest possible date, or are moved within the plan

findings.headline: Council received Exceptional Financial Support following Local Government Reorganisation and faces Fair Funding Review uncertainty
findings.detail: Following LGR, the council applied for and received Exceptional Financial Support (EFS), indicating prior financial distress. It now faces additional uncertainty from the Fair Funding Review, which could further impact funding. The council remains dependent on an externally-chaired Improvement Panel to exercise financial control.
findings.matters: Prior need for EFS and ongoing funding uncertainty means the council has limited financial resilience; Fair Funding Review could force further difficult decisions.
findings.figures: EFS application and approval; Fair Funding Review impact unknown
findings.quote: Due to the number of challenges faced following LGR, including around financial sustainability, the Council applied for Exceptional Financial Support to enable transformation of services. As the Council faces further challenges from reduced funding, including the Fair Funding Review, it remains crucial to monitor and review these actions

findings.headline: Office of the Transport Commissioner identified non-compliance with Council's Operating Licence
findings.detail: Correspondence from the Office of the Transport Commissioner identified areas of non-compliance with the Council's Operating Licence. This represents formal regulatory finding requiring remediation.
findings.matters: Transport compliance failure indicates documentation and process control issues; regulatory notices multiply during periods of management distraction.
findings.figures: Non-compliance identified; correspondence received
findings.quote: Correspondence from the Office of the Transport Commissioner identified areas of non-compliance with the Council's Operating Licence.

findings.headline: Ambitious capital programme for 2026/27 requires robust monitoring to identify and mitigate risks to project delivery and grant funding
findings.detail: The council has approved an ambitious capital programme for 2026/27 with significant activity planned. The AGS explicitly flags the need for robust monitoring to identify risks to project budgets, delivery of benefits and potential loss of grant funding. Project assurance reviews and business case improvements are planned.
findings.matters: An ambitious capital programme requires execution capability; given documented finance function capacity constraints, delivery risk is elevated.
findings.figures: "ambitious capital programme for 2026/27 with significant activity planned"
findings.quote: The council has approved an ambitious capital programme for 2026/27 with significant activity planned to progress major and capital projects in 2026. Robust monitoring of capital project delivery in 2026/27 will be required to identify and mitigate risks to project budgets, delivery of benefits and potential loss of grant funding.

findings.headline: Voluntary redundancy exercise across all council levels amid ongoing workforce capacity concerns
findings.detail: Following restructuring of the Extended Leadership Team in 2025/26, the council is embarking on a voluntary redundancy exercise across all service areas and organisational levels. This must be balanced against existing workforce capacity issues which were identified as a common theme in negative audit reports. Governance must be exercised to ensure VR does not undermine service delivery.
findings.matters: A council-wide VR exercise during a period of documented workforce capacity constraints and critical H&S compliance issues creates execution risk on service delivery and audit findings.
findings.figures: CEO restructured Extended Leadership Team; VR exercise across "all Council service areas and at all levels"
findings.quote: During the year 2025/26 the Chief Executive restructured his Extended Leadership Team, reducing the headcount. Work is now underway to commence a Voluntary Redundancy exercise across all Council service areas and at all levels of the organisation. The transformation programme and VR exercise must have regard to existing workforce capacity issues

findings.headline: Information Commissioner's Office issued Enforcement Notice on Freedom of Information request handling failures
findings.detail: The ICO issued a practice recommendation and subsequently an Enforcement Notice for failures in the council's handling of Freedom of Information requests. This represents formal regulatory enforcement action on information governance.
findings.matters: Regulatory enforcement indicates governance weakness and distraction during critical transformation; suggests compliance and documentation quality issues.
findings.figures: Practice recommendation escalated to Enforcement Notice
findings.quote: The Information Commissioner's Office issued a practice recommendation, and subsequently an Enforcement Notice, which identified failures in the Councils handling of Freedom of Information requests.

findings.headline: Health and Safety compliance risk escalated to critical following HSE inspections and external consultant review
findings.detail: Health and Safety Executive inspections identified failings in asbestos control and compliance with Control of Asbestos Regulations. An external consultant review also flagged health and safety governance concerns. The HSE is likely to issue an Improvement Notice. Risk was escalated to critical rating during 2025/26.
findings.matters: Critical H&S compliance failures expose the council to regulatory enforcement and reputational risk; they indicate management attention is split during financial stress.
findings.figures: Risk elevated to critical; HSE inspection findings; Improvement Notice expected
findings.quote: Of greatest concern during 2025/26 was the risks to workforce Health and Safety, which was increased to critical following reviews by internal audit, HSE and an external consultant. The Health and Safety Executive carried out a series of inspections to assess the Council's compliance with Control of Asbestos Regulations and identified failings which are likely to result in an Improvement Notice being issued against the Council

findings.headline: Two limited audit opinions in 2025/26 on Health and Safety governance and Asset Management Strategy
findings.detail: Internal audit delivered limited assurance opinions on Health and Safety (Governance) and Asset Management Strategy. Workforce capacity was identified as a common theme in negative internal audit reports throughout the year. These limited opinions indicate control weaknesses in critical operational areas.
findings.matters: Limited audit opinions signal control environment weakness and elevated operational risk, which lenders factor into credit assessment.
findings.figures: Two limited audit reports; workforce capacity "a common theme in internal audit reports during 2026/27"
findings.quote: Two limited audit reports were delivered in 2025/26: Health and Safety (Governance) and Asset Management Strategy. Workforce capacity remained a common theme in internal audit reports during 2026/27

findings.headline: Grant Thornton statutory recommendation in 2024/25 on finance function capacity to deliver accounts on time and ensure sustainability
findings.detail: External audit identified concerns about the Council's Finance function's capacity and capability to deliver statutory accounts within statutory deadlines and to ensure financial sustainability. This remains unresolved and is tracked in the Single Improvement Plan overseen by the externally-chaired Improvement Panel.
findings.matters: Statutory audit recommendations on finance function capacity directly impact financial reporting reliability and governance confidence.
findings.figures: 2024/25 recommendation, ongoing into 2025/26
findings.quote: The statutory recommendation issued by Grant Thornton in 2024/25 in relation to the capacity and capability of the Concil's Finance function in relation to its ability to deliver the accounts in line with statutory deadlines and ensure a financially sustainable Council.

findings.headline: Financial sustainability is the council's primary challenge with a balanced budget dependent on achieving savings targets
findings.detail: The council has agreed a balanced budget predicated on savings targets and must monitor outturn and savings achievement closely throughout 2026/27. Financial governance must be exercised around high-spend areas including agency workers and transformation projects. The council faces challenges from reduced funding including the Fair Funding Review.
findings.matters: A balanced budget dependent on savings execution is a core lending risk; failure to deliver savings cascades into reserves or overspend.
findings.figures: "balanced budget, predicated on savings targets"
findings.quote: Financial sustainability remains the Council's primary challenge going into 2025/26, particularly in relation to demand-led services. The Council has agreed a balanced budget, predicated on savings targets, and will need to continue to closely monitor the outturn position and achievement of savings targets throughout the year.

findings.paper_title: Item 10 - External Audit Progress Update Appendix
findings.headline: Reserves have no audit assurance for years with uncertain recovery through normal audit procedures.
findings.detail: Reserve balances are complex with no audit assurance for several years. The rebuild plan shows only partial assurance through 2029-30, with full assurance not expected until 2030-31. Grant Thornton states recovery may not even be achievable through standard procedures due to Local Government Reorganisation complexity and legacy body issues.
findings.matters: Reserves are a critical buffer for financial stability. Inability to audit reserves for years means the council's true financial position, liquidity, and ability to absorb shocks cannot be independently verified.
findings.figures: No assurance until 2028-29; partial assurance 2028-2030; full assurance 2030-31
findings.quote: With the exception of earmarked reserves, these reserves are complex and have no audit assurance for several years... it may not be possible to recover assurance over these balances through audit procedures alone.

findings.paper_title: Item 10 - External Audit Progress Update Appendix
findings.headline: Finance team lacks recent audit experience and must implement new ledger system during rebuild.
findings.detail: The finance team have not undergone a full audit process in several years and must make working papers audit-ready while handling queries under tight timescales. Separately, the council plans to implement a new financial ledger system during the rebuild period.
findings.matters: Finance team capacity determines whether the rebuild timeline is achievable. Implementing major systems during an active audit creates substantial risk of further delays and accounting errors.
findings.figures: No full audit process in several years; ledger system implementation during build-back period
findings.quote: The finance team have not undergone a full audit process in several years. Working papers need to be made audit-ready, and the finance team will need to find capacity to handle audit queries during the tight timescales. The Council also plans to implement a new financial ledger system during the build-back period, which poses a further capacity challenge.

findings.paper_title: Item 10 - External Audit Progress Update Appendix
findings.headline: Five-year recovery timeline: no clean audit opinion until 2030-31.
findings.detail: The audit trajectory shows disclaimed opinions through 2028-29, a qualified opinion in 2029-30, and first clean opinion in 2030-31. This assumes the 2025-26 and 2026-27 audits progress as planned. The auditor describes the path as 'a long route back to a clean audit opinion.'
findings.matters: A five-year timeline to audit assurance is unprecedented in local government and indicates severe structural deficiencies. Until 2030-31, the council's financial position will have no independent verification.
findings.figures: Clean audit opinion expected 30 November 2031; disclaimers through 2028-29
findings.quote: Given the challenging history of the lack of audit work able to be work performed at the Council and some of the legacies authorities which formed the Council, it is a long route back to a clean audit opinion at the Council.

findings.paper_title: Item 10 - External Audit Progress Update Appendix
findings.headline: Category D assessment: the worst rating due to major systemic problems in financial reporting.
findings.detail: Grant Thornton assessed Cumberland as Category D under the MHCLG capacity framework—indicating risk of not achieving an ISA-compliant audit by 2027-28 due to major systemic problems. This reflects the council's inability to produce accounts on time for two consecutive years, preventing any audit work.
findings.matters: Category D signals fundamental deficiencies in finance systems and controls, not merely operational difficulties. It suggests the council's financial reporting function is substantially broken.
findings.figures: Category D rating; no audit work possible 2023-24 or 2024-25
findings.quote: we have provisionally assessed this audit as Category D. This is due to the lack of audit work that has been possible in the first two years of the Council's existence (due to late drafting of the 2023-24 and 2024-25 accounts) and also a lack of audit assurance over some of the legacy local authorities that formed the Council.

findings.paper_title: Item 10 - External Audit Progress Update Appendix
findings.headline: Consecutive years of disclaimed audit opinions with no financial assurance pending.
findings.detail: Cumberland received disclaimed audit opinions for 2023-24 and 2024-25, meaning the auditor could not obtain sufficient evidence to form any opinion. The 2025-26 audit is also expected to be disclaimed. A disclaimer represents complete absence of audit assurance on the financial statements.
findings.matters: Lenders cannot independently verify the council's accounts through external audit. This eliminates the primary mechanism for assessing creditworthiness and prevents normal financial analysis.
findings.figures: Disclaimed opinions for years ended 31 March 2024 and 2025; 2025-26 also expected to be disclaimed
findings.quote: we do not expect to be able to support an unmodified (clean) opinion on the 2025-26 financial statements. Our audit focus is on 2025-26 in-year transactions and closing balances

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit of Finance Team Capacity & Delivery of Savings
findings.headline: Three high-priority audit findings all centre on savings governance and financial accountability
findings.detail: Of eight total recommendations (three high, five medium), all three high-priority findings relate to savings delivery: in-year validation (Rec 4), formal review and challenge of forecasts (Rec 7), and lessons-learned processes (Rec 8). This concentration signals that savings delivery is the audit's core concern.
findings.matters: The audit has identified systemic weaknesses in the council's ability to track and validate the savings that underpin its medium-term financial plan. This is the mechanism by which the council claims it will achieve balance.
findings.figures: 3 high recommendations out of 8 total; all on savings delivery and governance
findings.quote: The importance of addressing the high-graded recommendations outlined in section 7.2 cannot be understated. The Council faces ongoing well-documented financial pressures, which requires a robust monitoring and challenge process for savings if it is to continue to deliver a balanced budget.

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit of Finance Team Capacity & Delivery of Savings
findings.headline: No documented scrutiny or analysis when savings targets are not met
findings.detail: Where planned savings have failed to materialise, there is no evidence that responsible officers have analysed underlying reasons or that senior management has applied formal challenge. The audit identifies this as a high-priority issue requiring both enhanced formal review processes and a lessons-learned framework.
findings.matters: Without understanding why savings fail, the council cannot fix systemic forecasting problems. This suggests savings assumptions may be systematically optimistic.
findings.figures: High-graded Recommendations 7 and 8; no documented evidence currently exists
findings.quote: Where planned savings targets have not been achieved, there is no documented evidence of robust financial scrutiny, including analysis comparing forecast savings against actual outturn. There is limited evidence to demonstrate that responsible officers have undertaken sufficient analysis to identify, understand, and explain the underlying reasons where forecast savings have not materialised as anticipated.

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit of Finance Team Capacity & Delivery of Savings
findings.headline: No formal in-year validation that planned savings are actually being delivered
findings.detail: The council relies on quarterly forecasts rather than in-year evidence of actual savings achieved. Where savings adjustments are made, they happen through informal discussions between Finance and Programme teams without formal documentation. This is flagged as a high-priority recommendation requiring enhanced formal processes.
findings.matters: If the council cannot verify that savings are landing in-year, its MTFP is at risk. Forecasts versus actuals divergence could mean budget positions are worse than reported.
findings.figures: High-graded Recommendation 4; quarterly monitoring currently in place, monthly monitoring to be introduced
findings.quote: Quarterly monitoring reports provide visibility of forecast savings, the current arrangements do not allow for robust in year validation of actual savings achieved. Reported savings rely on forecasts and informal discussions rather than structured evidence-based tracking.

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit of Finance Team Capacity & Delivery of Savings
findings.headline: Council missed the statutory backstop deadline for publishing 2023-24 accounts
findings.detail: The council failed to publish its 2023-24 draft accounts within the statutory deadline, partly due to insufficient finance staff capacity during 2023-24 and the need to complete legacy accounts. External Auditors concluded the council did not have proper arrangements in place for economy, efficiency and effectiveness in use of resources.
findings.matters: Missing statutory deadlines is a red flag for financial governance and raises questions about whether the finance team can reliably deliver critical reporting.
findings.figures: 2023-24 accounts; statutory deadline missed
findings.quote: The Council was unable to publish its 2023-24 draft accounts in a timely manner and missed the statutory backstop deadline, though this is partly attributable to the significant number of legacy accounts the Council's Finance team had to first complete.

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit of Finance Team Capacity & Delivery of Savings
findings.headline: Audit gives only partial assurance on financial controls, the second-lowest rating
findings.detail: The report concludes that financial sustainability controls provide 'partial assurance' rather than substantial or comprehensive. The audit identifies multiple weaknesses across governance, savings tracking, and capacity that collectively expose the council to significant risks around financial sustainability.
findings.matters: Partial assurance means the council's internal control framework is insufficient and applies inconsistently. For a lender, this indicates elevated financial governance risk.
findings.figures: Partial assurance (versus five-point scale: comprehensive, substantial, reasonable, partial, limited/none)
findings.quote: From the areas examined and tested as part of this audit review, we consider the current controls operating within Financial Sustainability (Accountability and Capacity) provides partial assurance.

findings.headline: Council disputes auditor's Category D assessment as premature and disproportionately weighted to historical circumstances
findings.detail: Management argues the assessment underestimates current organisational capability. The council notes it delivered draft accounts on time, has invested in strengthening financial processes post-Local Government Reorganisation, is engaging constructively with auditors, and has yet to show inability to support a full audit as the 2025/26 process only recently commenced.
findings.matters: A disagreement between management and external auditors on audit risk severity could affect audit trajectory, timing to full compliance, and regulatory confidence in the council's trajectory.
findings.figures: None
findings.quote: Whilst the external auditor's assessment is understandably influenced by the absence of completed audit work in previous years, the Council considers that the classification places disproportionate weight on historical circumstances rather than current organisational capability.

findings.headline: External auditor provisionally assessed Cumberland as Category D—the highest risk category in the national regaining assurance framework
findings.detail: Category D indicates risk that fully compliant audit may not be achievable by 2027/28 due to major systemic issues. Grant Thornton cited no substantive audit work in the first two years, limited inherited assurance, treating 2025/26 effectively as a first-year audit, uncertainty about ISA-compliance capability, and implementing a new finance system during rebuild.
findings.matters: Category D suggests fundamental systemic challenges that could prevent the council achieving compliant audited accounts by the 2027/28 deadline, affecting borrowing decisions and regulatory confidence.
findings.figures: Category D (highest of four categories: A, B, C, D)
findings.quote: Grant Thornton has provisionally assessed Cumberland Council as Category D. The principal reasons cited are: No substantive audit work having been completed in the Council's first 2 years; Limited cumulative audit assurance inherited from predecessor authorities; The need to treat the 2025/26 audit effectively as a first-year audit; Uncertainty regarding the authority's ability to support a full ISA-compliant audit process because this has not yet been demonstrated in the new authority environment, and The additional challenge of implementing a new finance system during the build-back period

findings.headline: Cumberland received disclaimer audit opinions for its first two years of operation
findings.detail: The council cannot have its accounts audited for two years under normal audit standards. Following disclaimer opinions, auditors must rebuild assurance incrementally across property assets, pension liabilities, reserves, lease liabilities, working balances, and routine areas, which will require sustained commitment over multiple audit cycles.
findings.matters: Disclaimer audit opinions mean the council's financial statements received no audit assurance—a fundamental governance failure that affects creditworthiness and regulatory standing.
findings.figures: Two years of disclaimer opinions
findings.quote: Cumberland Council received disclaimer audit opinions for its first two years of operation and therefore falls within the scope of the national regaining assurance programme.

findings.paper_title: Annual Head of Internal Audit Opinion - 2025.26
findings.headline: Audit scope limitation on Risk Management and Counter-Fraud functions
findings.detail: The Head of Internal Audit notes an explicit limitation in scope regarding Risk Management and Counter-Fraud administrative responsibilities, meaning audit assurance does not cover these areas comprehensively.
findings.matters: Incomplete audit coverage of fraud and risk management functions compounds the partial assurance rating and leaves blind spots on key control areas.
findings.figures: scope limitation affecting Risk Management and Counter-Fraud
findings.quote: A limitation in scope, relating to Internal Audit & Risk Management's administrative responsibilities for Risk Management and Counter-Fraud is stipulated in section 3.

findings.paper_title: Annual Head of Internal Audit Opinion - 2025.26
findings.headline: External regulators have issued warnings and enforcement notices identifying significant weaknesses
findings.detail: The report explicitly states that external regulators have issued warnings and enforcement notices that identify areas of significant weakness in the council's systems, going beyond the internal audit findings.
findings.matters: External enforcement action signals serious control problems requiring urgent remediation and is a material credit event for lenders.
findings.figures: warnings and enforcement notices (unspecified)
findings.quote: a number of warnings and enforcement notices from external regulators identify areas of significant weakness.

findings.paper_title: Annual Head of Internal Audit Opinion - 2025.26

findings.detail: The annual opinion rates the council's governance, risk management and internal control arrangements as providing only 'partial assurance' — below the standard 'reasonable assurance' expected of councils. This represents material control and governance gaps that require lender attention.
findings.matters: Partial assurance indicates the council has not maintained control frameworks to the standard expected, increasing risk for lenders and signalling the finance director faces unresolved control issues.

findings.quote: The Head of Internal Audit's opinion of partial assurance on the Council's overall systems of governance, risk management and internal control for the year ended 31 March 2026.

findings.committee: Business and Resources Overview and Scrutiny Committee

findings.headline: Unplanned £2.881m reserve draw leaves only £4.631m buffer above minimum adequacy
findings.detail: The council required an unplanned £2.881m contribution from General Fund reserves to cover the year-end shortfall. This reduced reserves from £32.512m to £29.631m, leaving only £4.631m above the minimum adequacy level of £25.000m. findings.matters: Annual reserve draws for operational deficits indicate structural cash shortfalls; eroding reserves limits the council's ability to absorb future shocks or manage unexpected demand growth

findings.quote: The draft outturn position requires an unplanned contribution from General Fund balances of £2.881m. While this is still above the Adequacy of Reserves level of £25.000m, it is still reducing the level of General Fund available in 2026/27 for unplanned in-year demand or cost pressures.

findings.matters: Children in care are among the most expensive services; this sustained growth trajectory means the council faces structural demand pressures that cannot be managed through one-off efficiency measures

findings.detail: Two major savings programmes did not achieve targets: Our Future Cumberland shortfall of £4.596m and Customer Pre-Front Door shortfall of £3.000m. The council extended these via Exceptional Financial Support capitalisation but significantly reduced the PFD target to £0.500m for 2026/27 'to reflect what is still deliverable', indicating reduced confidence in programme delivery.
findings.matters: Transformation savings are critical to the council's medium-term financial plan; delays and downward reforecasts indicate the cost reduction strategy is at risk, creating structural budget pressure for future years

This surge is the primary driver of the £3.98m overspend in Home to School and SEND Transport and represents ongoing structural demand growth, not a one-off variance.
findings.matters: EHCP-related transport costs are demographic-driven and cannot be easily controlled; the council will require sustained budget increases to accommodate this trend unless policy changes

findings.matters: Unexplained or one-off budget allocations can mask underlying affordability problems or structural deficits; lenders require transparency on budget sustainability and the true cost of service delivery

findings.detail: External grant funding is heavily concentrated in 2026-27 (£186.3m) but falls to just £64.4m by 2029-30. These grants (Town Deal, Levelling Up, bus services, highways) are time-limited government schemes. The sharp decline means either capital spending must fall in later years or borrowing and reserves must increase further.
findings.matters: Lenders need to know whether the council has a credible plan for sustaining capital investment if government scheme funding ends, or whether outer-year plans are unaffordable

findings.detail: The capital programme requires £204.2m of prudential borrowing, heavily front-loaded at £113.9m in 2026-27, declining to £18.6m by 2029-30. This substantial debt assumption will require ongoing revenue budget servicing and constrains the council's future borrowing headroom.
findings.matters: Lenders need to assess whether the revenue budget can sustain debt servicing costs on £204m of new borrowing without crowding out service delivery or forcing future affordability crises

findings.detail: A residents survey in Autumn 2025, the first since the council's formation in 2023, found only 35% satisfied with how Cumberland Council runs things, against a national LGA average of 51%. Only 36% feel informed by the council about services and benefits (national average 49%), while 58% feel poorly informed (national average 49%). The report notes the national LGA satisfaction figure for 2025 is the lowest on record.
findings.matters: Resident satisfaction significantly below national average and declining trust in council communication may signal governance or service delivery concerns and could affect future political capital for difficult decisions.

findings.committee: Business and Resources Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Q4 Corporate Performance Report 202526_final draft
findings.headline: Severe health disparities: male life expectancy 2 years below England, suicide rate nearly double the national average
findings.detail: Male life expectancy in Cumberland is 77.8 years against a national average of 79.5 years. More critically, the suicide rate in Cumberland in 2022-24 was 19.4 per 100,000 population, almost double the England average of 10.9. The male suicide rate in Cumberland is 28.2 per 100,000 compared to 16.8 in England. Drug-related deaths are also significantly higher at 21.9 per 100,000 versus 8.8 in England.
findings.matters: Exceptionally high suicide and drug-death rates indicate severe population health challenges that will drive future demand for mental health and substance-abuse services.
findings.figures: 77.8 years male life expectancy (vs 79.5 England), 19.4 suicide rate per 100,000 (vs 10.9 England), 28.2 per 100,000 males (vs 16.8 England), 21.9 drug deaths per 100,000 (vs 8.8 England)
findings.quote: In the period 2022-24, there were 137 suicides in Cumberland (in people aged 10+ years) equating to a rate of 19.4 per 100,000, this is almost double the England average of 10.9. Men are at a greater risk of suicide with rates significantly higher in men than women both nationally and in Cumberland; the suicide rate in males in Cumberland is 28.2 per 100,000 (England 16.8).

The paper explicitly states 'there remains a risk that early help will continue to be drawn into complex work, and statutory demand will persist or grow.'
findings.matters: A structural shift of need from preventative early help to expensive statutory services (children's social care, adult social care) signals growing social pressures and future demand for more costly provision.
findings.figures: 296 children and young people in internal Early Help plans (Q4), ongoing restructure to rebalance system
findings.quote: The key strategic concern is that, despite positive early help metrics, demand is continuing to shift downstream into statutory and care services, indicating that system pressure is not reducing. This reflects a structural imbalance where limited early help capacity is increasingly focused on more complex, higher-threshold cases, reducing its effectiveness as a preventative layer. As a result, strong early help activity is not translating into reduced demand for Section 17 or cared-for children services.

findings.committee: Business and Resources Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: Budget planning depends on government funding settlement not yet announced
findings.detail: The council is awaiting an MHCLG policy statement on the Fair Funding Review outcome to clarify its 2026/27 funding position. Current financial planning relies on assumptions that cannot be finalized until the Provisional Local Government Finance Settlement is announced in December.
findings.matters: Major policy uncertainties delay the council's ability to finalize its position; a lender cannot assess financial sustainability until funding is known.

findings.committee: Business and Resources Overview and Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: A substantial budget gap remains for 2026/27 despite previous savings efforts
findings.detail: The council explicitly states it faces significant pressures from rising demand, inflation, and ongoing funding uncertainties. Previous savings and transformation efforts have not closed the gap, which the CFO describes as substantial but does not quantify.
findings.matters: Lenders need to know whether a council can close its budget gap through sustainable service changes or savings, or whether it will resort to unsustainable one-off measures.
findings.figures: No specific gap size provided
findings.quote: Despite previous savings and transformation efforts, a substantial budget gap remains for 2026/27.

findings.headline: IFRS 16 accounting change impact on borrowing limits not yet determined
findings.detail: Adoption of IFRS 16 leases accounting from 2024-25 affects recognition of lease and PFI arrangements. The council states this will impact prudential indicators including the Authorised Limit for External Debt and Operational Boundary. Work to quantify the impact remains in progress.
findings.matters: If IFRS 16 adds material lease liabilities to the balance sheet, it could consume available borrowing headroom under prudential code limits and require strategy adjustments. The magnitude is currently unknown.
findings.figures: Impact under quantification; affects Authorised Limit and Operational Boundary
findings.quote: Work to establish the impact of IFRS 16 remains in progress.

findings.headline: PWLB rate forecasts significantly overestimated rate falls; deferral strategy depends on forecast accuracy
findings.detail: The council's strategy to defer long-term borrowing was predicated on rates falling from elevated levels. However, actual PWLB rates at year-end diverged materially from mid-year forecasts: the 50-year rate forecast was 5.30% but came in at 5.67% (+37bp), and the 25-year was forecast 5.50% but came in at 5.98% (+48bp). Rates trended up, not down.
findings.matters: If rates remain elevated when the council's short-term borrowing comes due for refinancing, expected savings from deferral evaporate and refinancing costs rise materially. The council has placed a directional bet on rates that market conditions have already contradicted.
findings.figures: 50-year: forecast 5.30%, outturn 5.67%; 25-year: forecast 5.50%, outturn 5.98%
findings.quote: At 31 March 2025, the 50-year PWLB certainty rate (gilt plus 80bp) for new loans stood at 5.67% (fixed) compared to 5.13% at 30 September 2024.

findings.headline: £46m of borrowing due 12-24 months creates refinancing concentration risk
findings.detail: The council drew £45m in new PWLB loans in March 2025 with 1-2 year maturities, concentrating 16.35% of total borrowing into the near-term maturity window. The council acknowledges this creates a refinancing spike requiring careful monitoring as rates remain elevated against forecasts.
findings.matters: Concentration of debt maturities amplifies refinancing risk. If rates do not fall as the council expects, refinancing £46m in the next 24 months will occur at elevated cost, and the borrowing deferral strategy will have failed to deliver anticipated savings.
findings.figures: £45m new borrowing; 16.35% of total debt maturing 12-24 months (£46.2m)
findings.quote: The additional borrowing of £45m drawn down in 2024-25 with maturities of between one and two years, has also created a further spike in loan maturing in the shorter term. Whilst this position was anticipated and entirely consistent with the Council's approved borrowing strategy the inherent risks associated with this position will nonetheless require careful monitoring going forward.

findings.headline: Treasury control breach: £5m counterparty investment limit exceeded
findings.detail: In April 2025, the council placed a £15m fixed-term investment with SMBC Bank International that exceeded the approved £10m counterparty limit by £5m. The breach was identified and corrected on maturity in May. This represents a failure in treasury controls even though the breach was subsequently rectified.
findings.matters: Lenders rely on councils maintaining robust treasury management controls. A breach of counterparty limits indicates control weaknesses that could permit larger problems to develop undetected.
findings.figures: £5m breach: £15m invested against £10m approved limit
findings.quote: On this occasion the £15m upper limit for principal invested with this counterparty was exceed by £5m. This breach was identified and corrected on maturity.

news_drafts.headline: Council carrying unquantified Equal Pay claim relating to over 400 employees transferred from former County Council
news_drafts.lead: Equal pay claims can result in substantial backdated pay awards. An unquantified contingent liability is a hidden risk to the budget, particularly if the claim is settled while the council is managing large deficits.

news_drafts.headline: General Fund reserves are only just above minimum required; asset sales yield insufficient and behind schedule
news_drafts.lead: Low reserves with no buffer leaves the council vulnerable to any variance in spending or income. Asset sales are the only planned reserve replenishment and they are materializing slowly.

news_drafts.headline: SEND identified as 'the most significant long-term financial risk' with no fully implemented sufficiency solution
news_drafts.lead: SEND is nationally a growing cost pressure; a council admitting it lacks control suggests this line item will continue to be a budget pressure and potential overspend source.
